steps.content: Witness. Observe. Verify. The line between right and wrong is well-defined. If one commits a crime, they must be punished. There's no gray area between black and white. No one should get punished for doing something good. To me as a child, justice was just that simple.
What do you want to be when you grow up, kiddo?
The little girl stands on tiptoe and cranes her neck, so that she can speak into the microphone.

steps.speaker: Little Bianca
steps.content: I... I want to be a brave warrior like Super Apple!

steps.speaker: Little Bianca
steps.content: Super Apple is the strongest warrior in the world. He finds all the bad guys in hiding and brings them to justice. I want to be as awesome as Super Apple!
steps.female_content: Super Apple is the strongest warrior in the world. She finds all the bad guys in hiding and brings them to justice. I want to be as awesome as Super Apple!

steps.content: Have you thought about becoming a <color=#fb9259>reporter</color>?
The little girl ponders the question for a long while before answering.

steps.speaker: Little Bianca
steps.content: I, um, I don't understand. Can a reporter punish bad guys like Super Apple does?

Unfortunately, reporters don't have superpowers like Super Apple does. Being a reporter means working overtime, running around to do investigations, feeling defeated when the bad guys get the upper hand and escape scot-free.

steps.speaker: Little Bianca
steps.content: I see. In that case, I don't want to become a reporter. That's disappointing...
The girl looks crestfallen. To her mind, there's nothing awesome about being a reporter.
Having said that...

Sometimes, it's hard to tell who are the bad guys, who are the good guys, because some bad guys are cunning, and they pretend to be good guys and live among us. So even Super Apple, though very powerful, wouldn't know where to land punches.
That's where we eagle-eyed reporters come in! We make the bad guys show their true colors. That way, Super Apple knows who they are and where to find them, and then...
Bang, bang! Kicks their behinds!
Exposing the bad guys! That's the first step in bringing them to justice.
Young Bianca is so caught up in the moment that she, mimicking her favorite cartoon superhero, starts punching the air, a sparkle of excitement in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Little Bianca
steps.content: Wow! That's so cool, so awesome!

steps.speaker: Little Bianca
steps.content: I've made up my mind! I want to—

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: —I want to win the Best News Award and become the number one reporter in Eastside!
A deafening silence follows Bianca's bold statement.

steps.speaker: Interviewer A
steps.content: We're glad to hear about your aspirations, but could you introduce yourself first?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Oh, sorry, sorry, I got carried away.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Hello, my name is Bianca. I graduated from the School of Journalism at the Communication University of Eastside. My dream is to become a reporter, win the Best News Award, and expose all evil deeds that deserve to be punished. Here are my internship certificates and a record of the hands-on experience I've gained in the field of journalism.
After a Q&A session, Bianca thanks the two interviewers for their time and leaves the room. It takes a moment for the interviewers to recover from exposure to her rapid-fire speech.

steps.speaker: Interviewer B
steps.content: The candidate has impressive internships, with a unique way of looking at things, plus her writing is solid. A bit too enthusiastic, but that can be a good trait in a reporter.

steps.speaker: Interviewer A
steps.content: That settles it then.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: I'm done for. I can't squeeze another word out of me.

steps.speaker: Morghan
steps.content: Hmm...

steps.speaker: Morghan
steps.content: Hey, is she drinking "juice" on the job again?

steps.speaker: Ethan
steps.content: Unfortunately, not today. She just got another proposal rejected by the editor-in-chief. Her fourth this week. She's racking her brains for a fifth.
Bianca raises a limp hand.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: This is my sixth, actually.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Being a reporter will be the death of me. I have half a mind to return to my hometown and become an apple grower...
Morghan flicks the apple on Bianca's headband and pulls out the notebook from under her arms. It's crammed with notes.

steps.speaker: Morghan
steps.content: Alright, let me take a look. Maybe I can help. Hidden Truth About Overpriced Nutrient Drink. Good heavens, where did you dig up such a niche topic?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: "Unleash the untapped potential of your brain! Effective after one week of continuous use!" Sounds cool, huh? Well, guess what? This so-called elixir is just water with some low-quality additives in it.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: The editor-in-chief says there are already too many reports on snake oil scams out there, and asks me to think of another topic.

steps.speaker: Morghan
steps.content: What about this one, Investigation into FAC Embezzlement?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: The editor-in-chief said, and I quote, "Good topic, but it's dangerous territory. You wouldn't want the station to be shut down, would you?"

steps.speaker: Morghan
steps.content: And this one, Old Scavenger Claims Abandoned Factory is Haunted?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: I killed this one myself. I had thought there was something newsworthy behind it, like a conspiracy or something. Turned out it was just a farce. Rounding up delinquent teenagers in the street for littering would've been more fun.
Morghan shoves the notebook on Bianca's face.

steps.speaker: Morghan
steps.content: Stop complaining. Be glad you have something to write about. Beggars can't be choosers.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: What's the point in covering such farces? To me, being a reporter means facing reality head-on, even if it can be harsh sometimes, and uncovering hidden evils in everyday life and exposing them to the world.

steps.speaker: Ethan
steps.content: If there are no big stories to report on, doesn't that mean we're living in a peaceful society? That's a good thing.

steps.speaker: Ethan
steps.content: The editor-in-chief is strict with you, but that's for your own good, too. Some stones are best left unturned, or you risk getting stung by whatever is hiding underneath. You've got a long career ahead of you; it's not worth it.
Clearly, the young reporter is not convinced. She grabs the notebook and starts flipping through it, muttering under her breath.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: It's simply unacceptable to me, wrongdoers walking around among decent people like nothing has happened. There is so much filth around us, and some people just look the other way as if it weren't there.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Are we supposed to turn a blind eye to injustices? No, that's not right!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Wrongdoers must be punished. If other reporters don't want to step up...

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Then I'll take the first step toward justice!
The scene freezes, and everyone becomes motionless, as if someone has pressed pause.

Witness. Observe. Verify. To me back then, what a reporter did was no different from me, as a kid, denouncing the misdeeds of other kids with a loudspeaker. I showed bad guys up for who they really were, then saw them get punished. In my eyes, that was justice. As simple as that. That was what drove me to sneak into the factory with ${PlayerName}. I thought that when I found evidence and posted it online, defenders of justice would come and punish the wrongdoers. But... they never came.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Wait, what does it mean?

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: It means that you're to stop your investigation into the case regarding the leakages of online information, no matter how far you've gotten. Effective immediately.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Why?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: The lowlifes who leaked the personal information of their victims have been arrested. What we need to do next is publish the article I'm working on and make an effort to put public opinion back on track, and then...

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: Bianca!

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: How many articles have you published about this case?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Four.

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: During this time, did the online discussion on this case change in any way because of your articles? Did those people with the strongest opinions click on your articles and have a read?

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: Let's look at the practical side of this matter. You and I both know that the guys who got caught are just the tip of the iceberg. We have no idea how many more of these people are hiding in the dark corners of the internet. Can you catch them all?

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: No, at least not as a reporter.

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: Bianca, you're a smart person, and a smart person should know their limits.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: So there isn't anything else I can do about it?

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: There is.

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: Drop this case and work on something new.
Beep... Beep...

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Hello...

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: This is Bianca, the reporter who interviewed you. Do you remember me? Yes, yes, the one with the apple on her headband.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Mm-hmm, don't worry, everything's going smoothly. I... I've talked it over with my editor-in-chief. When the next article comes out, the people of DisCity will know you're innocent, and that the real bad guys are those who cyberbullied you.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: What? Someone posted your personal information on Gray Mirror again, and even started a vote on you? That's outrageous!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: I'm still investigating Gray Mirror, and I've found some clues about their server. One day, I'll expose those people who've been spreading rumors online about you. There will be justice.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Yes?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Ever since your address was leaked, there have been people turning up on your doorstep every day to harass you. I see... You've decided to move?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: You're breaking up. Hello, hello, is that the sound of a strong wind I'm hearing?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Wait, where are you right now?
A faint voice comes through the earpiece. Bianca puts two and two together, realizing with a sinking feeling where the person on the other end of the line is.

steps.speaker: Despairing Voice
steps.content: Thank you, thank you for speaking up for me. I'm sorry, but I can't take it anymore...

steps.speaker: Despairing Voice
steps.content: This is it for me. Thank you, Bianca.

steps.speaker: Despairing Voice
steps.content: Goodbye.
Bianca stands on the edge of the rooftop, looking down at the city, her face expressionless.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Would you like me to read you how they're "mourning" you?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Dead? It serves her right. What respectable person would chat on the dark web? Must have been desperate for fame!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Sorry, but I find it hard to feel sympathetic to girls who play the victim card. How could there be so many difficulties? They're just too fragile.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: And this one. LOL. You sure she's not playing possum? Wouldn't be surprised if she's back online a few days later to reap a crop of new followers. Hehe...

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Haha! These are just parasites who hide in the dark. Clearly, they have no idea it's dumb luck that they haven't been caught yet. They think they're invincible in the digital world.
As Bianca reads out the comments on the screen one by one, her voice grows increasingly intense and emotional.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Ah, what's the use of exposing the vermin? Defenders of justice are few and far between. Even if you drag the vermin out in the open, they'll just crawl their way back to the shadows, thriving like before, impossible to eradicate...

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: They enjoy "exposing" other people. Well, let's give them a taste of their own medicine. They have it coming!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Choose justice, administer justice! The intrepid reporter overcomes obstacles and obtains the power to confront the forces of evil. To protect the kind people of this city, she must eradicate all the vermin, leaving them no chance to come back!

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Dear fellow forum users, let's take a vote together. This is our chance to rewrite the ending, to reshape this revolting story into <color=#fb9259>its best possible form</color>.

User Extra-Rich Apple Juice 2.0 has been found to be spreading misinformation on the forum. This behavior has significantly eroded productive discussion within the forum community. On account of multiple reports from other users, all content posted under this account, including replies and comments, will now be removed from this site. In addition, Extra-Rich Apple Juice 2.0 is to be permanently banned from the forum. This ban is effective immediately and is not subject to appeals.
Bianca stares blankly and silently at the ban notification on the screen.
You sense acutely that Bianca's emotions are tempestuous, and that the Mania Flux around her is intensifying, about to exceed the safe range.

options: Bianca, get a hold of yourself!

choices.text: Bianca, get a hold of yourself!

steps.content: Take a deep breath and calm down. You're about to lose control of yourself.
You watch Bianca nervously, shackles at the ready. She doesn't look up, and it's a long time before she speaks again.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Ah, I've made life difficult for you again, haven't I? I promised to control my powers, and I broke my word again.
Bianca sounds as light-hearted and cheerful as when you first met her.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: I'm fine. This isn't the first time I've been banned. I'm already used to it.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: It's a sensitive topic. We should count ourselves lucky that the post stayed on the forum for as long as it did. A shame that the buzz disappeared like that, though. Reposting wouldn't make much difference now; the curious crowd must have already moved on to other posts.
Don't lose heart. We still have a chance—

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Have a chance to do what, Chief?
Bianca suddenly interrupts you.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: What should I do?

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: I observed injustice, I recorded it, I shouted it out for the world to hear. I've done all I can, but nothing has changed.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: Turns out the real world isn't black and white like cartoons. Super Apple can't rid the world of all bad guys. Each exposure only makes them better at hiding in darker shadows.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: No meaningful change has come of my efforts to expose them.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: My efforts have proved fruitless.
Finally, Bianca turns to you, wearing her usual smile.

steps.speaker: Bianca
steps.content: So tell me, Chief, what else I can do?
